comparison: Both evaluate calcium signaling claims (C3, C36-C39, C47-C49, C106) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed technical validation of R-GECO1 and Aequorin data with controls. Peer reviewers accept these findings as 'solid evidence' and 'elegant experiments.' Strong agreement on calcium imaging data quality.

OpenEval evaluates spatial Ca2+ patterns and receptor expression (C40-C46, C98) as SUPPORTED with mechanistic explanation. Peer review R1 includes overlapping claims (C40-C46) in their SUPPORTED evaluation of calcium data. Both accept the descriptive calcium imaging findings.

OpenEval evaluates developmental stage-specific calcium responses (C50-C57) as SUPPORTED. Peer review R1 includes overlapping claims (C50-C55) in their SUPPORTED evaluation. Both accept the temporal correlation data without challenge.

OpenEval finds ROS data (C4, C33-C35, C14) SUPPORTED with appropriate controls. Peer review rates these claims UNCERTAIN, noting limitations of overexpression lines and questioning whether outputs definitively represent immune/defense responses. Significant disagreement on interpretation despite accepting raw data.

Perfect claim overlap (C58-C64). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on multiple lines of evidence showing premature abscission phenotype. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, accepting genetic analyses as descriptive findings without challenge. Strong agreement.

Perfect claim overlap (C68-C74, C107). OpenEval rates stress-induced IDA expression as SUPPORTED with statistical validation. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 3 noting this provides 'valuable indication for potential involvement' beyond development. Strong agreement.

Perfect claim overlap (C75-C79) on callose deposition. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with appropriate controls and statistics. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN due to concerns about overexpression lines and physiological relevance. Disagreement on interpretation of overexpression data.

OpenEval evaluates defense gene induction (C82-C84, C88-C89) as SUPPORTED with statistical validation. Peer review R3 includes these claims but rates UNCERTAIN, questioning whether outputs definitively represent immune/defense responses versus developmental responses. Disagreement on functional interpretation.

OpenEval evaluates HAE/HSL2 receptor specificity data (C85-C87) as SUPPORTED, noting this demonstrates receptors are not sole mediators. Peer review R3 includes these claims in UNCERTAIN evaluation, concerned about classifying outputs as defense responses. Disagreement on mechanistic interpretation.

OpenEval evaluates IDA-flg22 synergy (C90-C93) as SUPPORTED with clear statistical demonstration. Peer review R3 includes these claims in UNCERTAIN evaluation, noting outputs are 'shared by multiple pathways' and questioning defense classification. Disagreement on specificity of response.

OpenEval evaluates overlapping receptor expression (C94-C95) as SUPPORTED by dual promoter-reporter analysis. Peer review R7 includes these claims with C96 and rates UNCERTAIN, accepting expression data but questioning mechanistic interpretation without functional validation. Partial disagreement.

Both address main conclusion about IDA's dual role (C96, C108-C109). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED as inference from convergent evidence. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, with reservations about definitively classifying outputs as immune/defense responses without pathogen assays. Significant disagreement on overall interpretation.

Strong claim overlap (C97, C99-C100). OpenEval rates mechanistic discussion as SUPPORTED though acknowledging speculation. Peer review R8 also rates SUPPORTED, accepting comparative analysis between IDA and flg22 signaling as 'elegant experiments.' Agreement on descriptive comparison.

Good claim overlap (C103-C105). OpenEval rates discussion of receptor coordination mechanisms as SUPPORTED though speculative. Peer review R9 also rates SUPPORTED, accepting analysis of published interaction data without challenge. Agreement on descriptive analysis.

OpenEval evaluates background claims (C1-C2, C6-C13) about established prior work as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focused on novel findings rather than background context.
OpenEval evaluates background claims (C14-C32) about ROS-Ca2+ signaling as SUPPORTED established knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though C14 appears in peer R2 context.
OpenEval evaluates background claims (C65-C67) summarizing prior IDA work as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focused on novel experimental findings.
OpenEval evaluates background claims (C80-C81) about defense gene markers as SUPPORTED established knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

Peer review evaluates ROS claims (C4, C33-C35, C14) as UNCERTAIN due to overexpression limitations and uncertainty about immune/defense classification. Corresponds to OpenEval R4 which rates SUPPORTED. Represents key disagreement area.

Peer review evaluates broad set of defense-related claims (C5, C82-C93, C108) as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether outputs definitively represent immune/defense responses. Overlaps with multiple OpenEval results (R8, R9, R10) that rate individual claim sets as SUPPORTED. Major interpretive disagreement.
